title: One allowance or one per panel?
hook: Six panels each need a 5cm allowance. Is one 5cm allowance enough?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Differentiate per-piece allowances from one-time allowances.

misconception: A per-piece allowance only needs to be added once.
objective: Differentiate per-piece allowances from one-time allowances.

claims.text: Each panel requires 1.20m plus a separate 0.05m allowance. Compare repeating the allowance with adding it once. Scaled model; length-only model; no cutting instructions.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Panels=6, A=7.5m and B=7.25m. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",1.25]; B=["+",["*","x",1.2],0.05]; x denotes Panels. At x=6, A=7.5, B=7.25. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. claims.text: An allowance attached to every panel is a per-unit term. Multiply both the main length and allowance by the panel count. Adding the allowance once treats it as a single job-level term.

The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.
